sentences.text: Diplocynodon was an extinct eusuchian crocodilian that lived in Europe, possessing a bony armor of osteoderms covering its neck, back, belly, and tail.
While some members of this genus could grow to three meters long, others remained smaller than one meter.
The largest known species, D. hantoniensis, measured 5.9 meters in length.
Many well-preserved specimens contain gastroliths, which are stones swallowed to help digest food.
The genus Diplocynodon was first described by Pomel in 1847.
Well-preserved specimens have been found in the Messel Pit and the Geiseltal lignite deposit in Germany.
Martin and colleagues reported in 2026 that fossil material was found in Oligocene strata in central Turkey.
Diplocynodon species are almost exclusively found in freshwater environments.
Researchers believe the various species were opportunistic aquatic predators.
Isotopic analysis of enamel from Late Oligocene specimens indicates Diplocynodon primarily fed on aquatic vertebrates.
Osteohistological analysis suggests D. hantoniensis had a growth pattern similar to the modern American alligator, with determinate, seasonally-controlled growth.
CT scans of D. tormis have reconstructed internal snout and brain structures, providing insights into its sensory and cognitive capabilities.
Skull shape analysis suggests Diplocynodon was a small generalist carnivore that shared resources with the larger Asiatosuchus.
Diplocynodon is considered one of the most basal members of the superfamily Alligatoroidea.
The type species of the genus Diplocynodon is Diplocynodon ratelii.
Fossils of Diplocynodon date from the Paleocene to the Middle Miocene.
During the Eocene, the Messel quarry was a freshwater swamp lake that was ideal for fossil preservation due to anoxic conditions at the bottom.
